newsitem.title: JAPAN: MITI minister says good if yen stabilises now.
newsitem.headline: MITI minister says good if yen stabilises now.

text.p: Japanese Trade Minister Shunpei Tsukahara said on Tuesday that he thought it would be good if the yen stabilises at around current levels.
"It would be good if it (the dollar/yen rate) stabilised around here," he said.
The dollar had surged to almost 115 yen in early Tokyo trade before easing back slightly. It stood at 114.55 yen in late Tokyo morning trade.
The dollar had risen on aggressive buying from domestic and overseas operators and remarks by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that he was not concerned about the dollar's recent rise.
But Tsukahara emphasised that stability is the most important factor in the foreign exchange market because corporations need time to adjust to currency fluctuations.
